messages:
Lena: Hey team — after bringing up the v2 quantized build of model-x the chat templates are broken. Short example: system prompt no longer terminated, responses glue into one line. Suspect special-token remap during HF->Redwood conversion.

Ajay.k: Can you paste the tokenizer added_tokens.json and the conversion log? That usually tells the story.

Lena: Pasting minimal snippets. HF added_tokens.json (from model repo):
```json
[{"content": "<|bos|>", "id": 50256}, {"content": "<|eos|>", "id": 50257}, {"content": "<|pad|>", "id": 0}, {"content": "<|unk|>", "id": 100}]
```
Conversion log (convert-bot):
```
convert-tool --from hf --to redwood --quant int8 --check-added-tokens
INFO: mapping added_tokens -> starting remap
WARN: found added_tokens without explicit ids, assigning sequential ids starting at 50256
INFO: finalized tokenizer vocab size 50260
```

Lena: But in the runtime tokenizer dump we see pad mapped to 50258 and bos to 0.

maria.s: That's the classic "sequential assign" bug when added_tokens.json items are objects vs list entries. HF expects ids but sometimes tokenizers serialize differently. Did the repo use list-of-strings or list-of-objects?

Lena: Model repo uses list-of-objects (we showed that). HF's tokenizer used explicit ids, but our conversion path apparently ignored the id field when quant flag is present (??) because conversion uses an optimized path.

convert-bot: automated note: we ran token id parity check: mismatches detected: bos expected 50256 got 0; eos expected 50257 got 50259; pad expected 0 got 50258; unk expected 100 got 100 (ok).

Ajay.k: That explains the template fallout — chat templates rely on bos/eos/pad ids for prefix/KV cache priming. If bos -> 0 (pad slot) then prefix tokens get treated as padding and trimmed.

Oliver.t: Quick workaround: we can remap the tokenizer on load by reading original added_tokens and forcing explicit ids before building tokenizer. I'll open a small script and a patch for the conversion tool.

Oliver.t: Proposed fix snippet:
```python
# remap_added_tokens.py
import json
at = json.load(open('added_tokens.json'))
for tok in at:
    if isinstance(tok, dict) and 'id' in tok:
        tokenizer.force_set_token_id(tok['content'], tok['id'])
```

maria.s: Also let's add a unit test: convert -> load -> dump -> diff should be idempotent. Add a CI job for quantized builds specifically; we missed this edge case because only full-precision conversion runs the id-parity test.

Lena: QA results: qa-bot reports eval regressions on standard chat-quality suite after the bad conversion run: response-coherence dropped 8% and prompt-truncation cases jumped from 0.2% -> 4.1%.

qa-bot: automated report: scoreboard v2-quantized-run-20240526.json attached (summary: coherence -8%, truncation +3.9%).

Ajay.k: Priority: hotfix for conversion pipeline + backfill token fix for recent models. Which models rolled out with the buggy path? Lena, can you enumerate?

Lena: model-x v2 (just onboarded), model-y edge branch (experimental). I'll collect commits and affected SHAs.

Oliver.t: I'll send the patch to conversion tool today and a follow-up PR to add the id-parity check into the quantized conversion CI.

maria.s: Good. Also add an assert that added_tokens objects have numeric ids and fail loudly if they don't match the HF tokenizer.ids map. Silent reassignment is the root cause.

Lena: Thanks. Can someone run a quick scanner to list models with non-empty added_tokens objects vs list-of-strings? I can triage which need immediate remap.

Ajay.k: I'll drop a small grep+python script in #eng-ml to scan model repos and open a tracking ticket in the tracker.

Lena: Great. For now rolling back the quantized endpoint to last known-good (fp16) to stop user impact. :thumbsup:

convert-bot: action: rollback initiated for model-x v2 (deploy id d-4921).

Oliver.t: Follow-up tasks: 1) patch conversion, 2) CI id-parity test for quantized path, 3) remap script + run on affected models, 4) postmortem note for onboarding checklist.

maria.s: I'll own the postmortem doc and add checklist items for future HF->Redwood conversions.

Lena: Thanks everyone. I'll update thread when I have the list of affected SHAs.
